purpose: Tetracycline is an antibiotic used to treat many types of bacterial infections, including acne, chest infections, urinary tract infections, and certain sexually transmitted infections. It can also be used for infections caused by unusual bacteria like Lyme disease or Rocky Mountain spotted fever. Your doctor may prescribe it when other antibiotics are not the best choice for your specific infection.
how_it_works: Tetracycline works by stopping bacteria from making the proteins they need to grow and multiply. Think of it like cutting off the bacteria's food supply — without those proteins, the bacteria cannot survive or spread. This gives your immune system the chance it needs to clear the infection from your body.
common_side_effects: The most common side effects include nausea, vomiting, stomach upset, and diarrhea. You may also notice sensitivity to sunlight, meaning you can sunburn much more easily than usual. Some people develop a headache or feel dizzy. Taking it with a full glass of water and staying upright for at least 30 minutes after each dose can help reduce stomach problems.
warnings: Do NOT take tetracycline with milk, dairy products, antacids, or iron supplements within 2 hours, as they block the medicine from working properly. This medication should NOT be used in children under 8 years old or during pregnancy because it can permanently stain developing teeth and harm bone growth. Always wear sunscreen and protective clothing while taking this medicine. Do not lie down right after taking it, as it can cause serious irritation or ulcers in your esophagus (food pipe).
typical_dosing: The usual adult dose is 250 mg to 500 mg taken by mouth 2 to 4 times a day, depending on your infection. It is best taken on an empty stomach — about 1 hour before meals or 2 hours after eating — with a full glass of water. Always finish the entire course of antibiotics your doctor prescribed, even if you start feeling better sooner.
